Mujahid said: The meaning of ﴿Why have You raised me blind?﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:125] is: "I have no proof, although I was knowledgeable of my proof and perceptive of it, and I used to argue on my own behalf in the world." End of quote. The servant asked his Lord about the cause that made it deserved for him to be raised blind, because he was ignorant of it and thought he had no sin. So the One whose remembrance is exalted said to him: ﴿Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them, and thus today you are forgotten﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:126]. That is: "Likewise you are." Then He explained that Our signs came to you clear and luminous, but you did not look at them with the eye of one who takes heed, you did not perceive, you abandoned them and became blind to them. So today We will leave you in your blindness and will not remove its covering from your eyes. This is what al-Zamakhshari said. The word "forgetting" here means "abandoning," not "heedlessness." The meaning of "you are forgotten" is "you are left (to suffer) in punishment." ﴿And thus We recompense﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:127], that is, with a similar recompense, ﴿those who transgress﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:127], that is, those who exceed the limit in disobedience. Then God, exalted is He, informed that the punishment of the Hereafter is "more severe," that is, than the punishment of this world, because it is greater than it, "and more lasting," that is, because it is permanent and continuous, whereas the punishment of this world is terminated. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Being raised on blindness that never ends forever is more severe than the hardship of a life that comes to an end. Or he meant: our leaving him in blindness is more severe and more lasting [p. 288] than his leaving our signs."

﴿Has it not guided them how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:128]. ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:129]. ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day, that perhaps you may be pleased﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:130]. ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, to test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:131]. ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you, and the best outcome is for piety﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:132]. ﴿And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:133]. ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we would follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:134]. ﴿Say, "Each is waiting, so wait; you will soon know who are the companions of the even path and who has been guided"﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:135].

The majority of readers read (yahdi) with the letter ya' (ي). A group among them, including Ibn Abbas and al-Sulami, read it with the letter nun (ن) (nahdi). God rebuked them and reminded them of lessons from the generations that came before them. By "destruction" is meant the destruction resulting from denying the messengers, abandoning faith in God, and not following His messengers. The subject of (yahdi) is a pronoun referring back to God, exalted is He, and this interpretation is supported by the reading (nahdi) with nun, meaning "We make clear," as al-Zajjaj said. It was also said that the subject is implied, its estimate being "the guidance, the opinions, the reflection, and the consideration." Ibn Atiyya said: "This is the best of what I find it can be estimated." End of quote. This is also the view of al-Mubarrad, but it is not good, because it involves deleting the grammatical subject (fa'il), which is not permitted according to the Basrians. Its better form is to say that the subject is a concealed pronoun, its estimate being (yahdi) "he," that is, "the guidance." Abu al-Baqa' said: The subject is what is indicated by (ahlakna, "We destroyed"), and the clause is explanatory of it. Al-Hawfi said: ﴿How many We destroyed﴾ already indicates the destruction of the generations, so the estimate is: "Did We not make clear to them the destruction of those whom ﴿We destroyed﴾ from the generations, and the erasure of their traces, so that they might take warning from that?"

Al-Zamakhshari said: The subject of ﴿Has it not guided﴾ is the clause that follows it. He means: "Has it not guided them to this, by its meaning and content?" A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ [al-Saffat 37:78], ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat 37:79]. That is: "We left this statement for him." It is also permissible that the pronoun in it refers to God or to the Messenger. End of quote. That the clause is the subject is the view of the Kufan grammarians. As for his comparison and parallel with His saying, ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ [al-Saffat 37:78], ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat 37:79], the phrase "we left for him" carries the meaning of "saying," so the clause is reported with it, as if it were said: "We said regarding him," and we applied this phrase to him. A clause may be reported in the sense of saying just as it is reported in its own wording. The best of these interpretations is the first, namely that the subject is a pronoun referring back to God, as if He said: "Has not God made clear," and the object of "made clear" is omitted, that is, the lessons from the destruction of the earlier generations. Then He said ﴿How many We destroyed﴾, that is, "We destroyed many," so (kam) is the object of (ahlakna), and the clause is as if it explains the omitted object of (yahdi).

Al-Hawfi said: Some said it is in the position of the nominative case as the subject of (yahdi), and this was rejected against the one who said it, because the interrogative (kam) is not governed by what precedes it. End of quote. Here (kam) is not interrogative but declarative (khabariyya).

Abu al-Baqa' said: ﴿Yahdi lahum﴾ has two possibilities for its subject. One is a pronoun for the name of God, exalted is He, that is, "Has God not made clear to them?" And (yahdi) was made to take an object clause (ta'liq) here, since it has the meaning of "knows," as it was made to in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾ [Ibrahim 14:45]. End of quote.

And (kam) here is declarative, and a declarative (kam) does not cause the governing verb to be suspended (ta'liq), but the interrogative does. Ibn al-Sumayfa' read (yumassuna) with doubling and in the passive form, because the dual walks step by step, movement by movement, and stillness by stillness, so the passive form suited it. The pronoun in (yamshuna, "they walk") refers back to what it referred to in (lahum), namely the disbelievers who are being rebuked, meaning the Quraysh. The Arabs move about in the lands of 'Ad and Thamud and the peoples past which the Quraysh passed on their way to Syria and elsewhere, witnessing the traces of their destruction. ﴿Through whose dwellings they walk﴾ is a clause in the position of a circumstantial phrase (hal) from the pronoun in (lahum), and the governing verb is (yahdi). That is: "Did We not make clear to the polytheists, while they were walking through the dwellings of those disbelievers who were destroyed?" It was also said that it is a circumstantial phrase from the object of (ahlakna), meaning: "We destroyed them while they were secure, free to roam and to dispose of their dwellings, and nothing prevented them from enjoyment and disposal, whether sickness or anything else, so the destruction came upon them suddenly, while they were heedless of it."

﴿Indeed, in that﴾, that is, in that making clear through the destruction of the past generations, ﴿are signs for people of intellect﴾, that is, sound minds. Then God, exalted is He, explained the reason why the punishment is not hastened upon those who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ). The "word that preceded" is that which was established by delaying their recompense until the Hereafter. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar 54:46]. You say: "Had it not been for this promise, the like of Our destruction of 'Ad and Thamud would have been inevitable for these disbelievers." The word (lizam, "inevitable") is either a verbal noun of (lazama, "to be inseparable") used as a description, or it is a pattern (fi'al) with the meaning of (muftil, "compelling"), as if it were an instrument of necessity, and its form is like "lizaz khasm" (the strong clinging of an opponent). Abu 'Abdullah al-Razi said: There is no doubt that the "word" is God's information to His angels and His books on the Preserved Tablet, that the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), even if they deny, will be postponed, and they will not be treated as others were treated with total annihilation. End of quote.

As for "the specified term," it may be the term of their lives, or the term of their destruction in this world, or the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. These are sayings. According to the first, the punishment is what they will meet in their graves and after. According to the second, it is their being killed by the sword on the Day of Badr. According to the third, it is the punishment of Hell. In Sahih al-Bukhari it is related that the Day of Badr is the "inevitable" (al-lizam), and it is the Great Assault (al-batshah al-kubra). Apparently "and a specified term" is coordinated with "a word," and the coordinated element is placed after what it is coordinated with, and it is separated from it by the answer to (law la, "had it not been for"), for the sake of matching the rhyme-endings of the verses. Al-Zamakhshari permitted that "and a specified term" be coordinated with the concealed pronoun in (kana, "it would have been"). He said: That is, "it would have been" the immediate seizure and the specified term being two inevitable consequences, just as they were inevitable for 'Ad and Thamud. The specified term does not stand alone apart from the immediate seizure. End of quote.

That is: "We left this statement for him." It is also permissible that the pronoun in it refers to God or to the Messenger. End of quote. That the clause is the subject is the view of the Kufan grammarians. As for his comparison and parallel with His saying, ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ [al-Saffat 37:78], ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat 37:79], the phrase "we left for him" carries the meaning of "saying," so the clause is reported with it, as if it were said: "We said regarding him," and we applied this phrase to him. A clause may be reported in the sense of saying just as it is reported in its own wording. The best of these interpretations is the first, namely that the subject is a pronoun referring back to God, as if He said: "Has not God made clear," and the object of "made clear" is omitted, that is, the lessons from the destruction of the earlier generations. Then He said ﴿How many We destroyed﴾, that is, "We destroyed many," so (kam) is the object of (ahlakna), and the clause is as if it explains the omitted object of (yahdi).

Al-Hawfi said: Some said it is in the position of the nominative case as the subject of (yahdi), and this was rejected against the one who said it, because the interrogative (kam) is not governed by what precedes it. End of quote. Here (kam) is not interrogative but declarative (khabariyya).

Abu al-Baqa' said: ﴿Yahdi lahum﴾ has two possibilities for its subject. One is a pronoun for the name of God, exalted is He, that is, "Has God not made clear to them?" And (yahdi) was made to take an object clause (ta'liq) here, since it has the meaning of "knows," as it was made to in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾ [Ibrahim 14:45]. End of quote.

And (kam) here is declarative, and a declarative (kam) does not cause the governing verb to be suspended (ta'liq), but the interrogative does. Ibn al-Sumayfa' read (yumassuna) with doubling and in the passive form, because the dual walks step by step, movement by movement, and stillness by stillness, so the passive form suited it. The pronoun in (yamshuna, "they walk") refers back to what it referred to in (lahum), namely the disbelievers who are being rebuked, meaning the Quraysh. The Arabs move about in the lands of 'Ad and Thamud and the peoples past which the Quraysh passed on their way to Syria and elsewhere, witnessing the traces of their destruction. ﴿Through whose dwellings they walk﴾ is a clause in the position of a circumstantial phrase (hal) from the pronoun in (lahum), and the governing verb is (yahdi). That is: "Did We not make clear to the polytheists, while they were walking through the dwellings of those disbelievers who were destroyed?" It was also said that it is a circumstantial phrase from the object of (ahlakna), meaning: "We destroyed them while they were secure, free to roam and to dispose of their dwellings, and nothing prevented them from enjoyment and disposal, whether sickness or anything else, so the destruction came upon them suddenly, while they were heedless of it."

﴿Indeed, in that﴾, that is, in that making clear through the destruction of the past generations, ﴿are signs for people of intellect﴾, that is, sound minds. Then God, exalted is He, explained the reason why the punishment is not hastened upon those who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ). The "word that preceded" is that which was established by delaying their recompense until the Hereafter. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar 54:46]. You say: "Had it not been for this promise, the like of Our destruction of 'Ad and Thamud would have been inevitable for these disbelievers." The word (lizam, "inevitable") is either a verbal noun of (lazama, "to be inseparable") used as a description, or it is a pattern (fi'al) with the meaning of (muftil, "compelling"), as if it were an instrument of necessity, and its form is like "lizaz khasm" (the strong clinging of an opponent). Abu 'Abdullah al-Razi said: There is no doubt that the "word" is God's information to His angels and His books on the Preserved Tablet, that the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), even if they deny, will be postponed, and they will not be treated as others were treated with total annihilation. End of quote.

As for "the specified term," it may be the term of their lives, or the term of their destruction in this world, or the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. These are sayings. According to the first, the punishment is what they will meet in their graves and after. According to the second, it is their being killed by the sword on the Day of Badr. According to the third, it is the punishment of Hell. In Sahih al-Bukhari it is related that the Day of Badr is the "inevitable" (al-lizam), and it is the Great Assault (al-batshah al-kubra). Apparently "and a specified term" is coordinated with "a word," and the coordinated element is placed after what it is coordinated with, and it is separated from it by the answer to (law la, "had it not been for"), for the sake of matching the rhyme-endings of the verses. Al-Zamakhshari permitted that "and a specified term" be coordinated with the concealed pronoun in (kana, "it would have been"). He said: That is, "it would have been" the immediate seizure and the specified term being two inevitable consequences, just as they were inevitable for 'Ad and Thamud. The specified term does not stand alone apart from the immediate seizure. End of quote.

Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to be patient with what the idolaters of Quraysh say. They are the ones to whom the pronoun refers in ﴿Did it not guide them?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 128]. They used to say ugly things which Allah has recorded in His Book. So He commanded him to be patient with their harm and to bear what comes from their bad conduct. He commanded him to glorify and praise Allah, and ﴿with the praise of your Lord﴾ is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: while you are praising your Lord. The apparent meaning is that he was commanded to glorify (tasbih) combined with praise (hamd). It may also be that the wording is intended, i.e. say: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah," or that the meaning is intended, namely declaring Him free of imperfection, clearing Him of evil, and praising Him with beautiful praise. Abu Muslim said: it is not far-fetched to take it as declaring Him far above imperfection and magnifying Him, and the meaning is: occupy yourself with glorifying Allah at these times. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: this view is closer to the apparent meaning and to what was mentioned before, because He first commanded him to be patient ﴿with what they say﴾ of denial and of manifesting disbelief and polytheism. It is fitting that he be commanded to declare Him free of what they say, so that he would be one who manifests that and calls to it. For this reason the verse gathers all the times. Or the metaphorical sense may be intended, so that the meaning is prayer: before the rising of the sun is the Dawn prayer, before its setting is the Afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾ is the Maghrib and the 'Atama (Isha) prayers, and ﴿the ends of the day﴾ is the Dhuhr prayer alone. Ibn 'Atiyya said: the wording may also mean saying "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him" from after the Dawn prayer until the two rak'as of Duha, and before the setting of the sun. For the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever glorifies Allah at the setting of the sun seventy times, his sins will set with it." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿and before its setting﴾ means Dhuhr and 'Asr, because they fall in the latter half of the day, between the decline of the sun and its setting. The phrase ﴿during the hours of the night﴾ and ﴿the ends of the day﴾ is specifically devoted to these prayers, because the best remembrance is that at night, for the heart is gathered, the body is at rest, and one is alone with the Lord. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the rising at night﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 6], and He said: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], and the two verses. Also, because the night is a time of stillness and rest, when it is turned to worship it is harder and more burdensome on the self, and more exhausting and tiring for the body, so it is more fitting for the sense of obligation and more excellent in the sight of Allah. The glorification in ﴿during the hours of the night﴾ includes the 'Atama prayer, and ﴿the ends of the day﴾ includes the Maghrib and Fajr prayers, repeated for the purpose of specification, as the term was specified in His saying ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 238] according to some exegetes. End of quote. Here it says ﴿the ends of the day﴾, while in Hud it says ﴿and establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ [Hud: 114]. It was said: it came in the manner of the verse of poetry:

*"And two deserts, two sandy stretches, two times, whose backs are like the backs of shields."*

The dual came in its original form, and the plural is not confusing, since the day has only two ends. It was also said: the plural is in its literal sense, the Dawn is the first end, Dhuhr and 'Asr are from the second end, and the third end is Maghrib and 'Isha. It was also said: the day has four ends: at sunrise, at sunset, at the decline of the sun, and at its standing still before the decline. It was also said: Dhuhr is at the end of the first end of the day and the beginning of the last end, so it falls in two ends of it, and the third end is the setting of the sun, which is the time of Maghrib. It was also said: the day is taken as a genus, so each day has an end, and it repeats with the repetition of the day. It was also said: what is meant by the ends are the hours, because a tarf is the last part of a thing. Al-Jumhur read ﴿wa-atraafa﴾ with a fatha on the fa', as coordinated with ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾. It was also said: it is coordinated with ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾. Al-Hasan and 'Isa ibn 'Umar read ﴿wa-atraafi﴾ with a kasra on the fa', coordinated with ﴿aana'i﴾ (hours).

﴿So that you may be pleased﴾, meaning: you will be rewarded for these deeds with the reward you will see, and this is expressed in the form of hope and expectation, not as certainty. It was said: "la'alla" from Allah is obligatory. Abu Haywa, Talha, al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr, Aban, 'Isma, Abu 'Imara from Hafs, Abu Zayd from al-Mufaddal, Abu 'Ubayd, and Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Isbahani read ﴿turda﴾ with a damma on the ta', meaning: your Lord will please you.

* *

When Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to be patient and to glorify, the prohibition came against extending the gaze toward what the disbelievers have been given to enjoy. It is said: he extended his gaze toward what the disbelievers were given to enjoy, meaning he continued to look at it and reflected upon its whole and its details. It was said: the meaning according to this is: do not marvel, O Muhammad, at what We have given them to enjoy of wealth, sons, dwellings, mounts, garments, and foods, for all of that is like a flower that has no permanence or lasting, and it will soon perish and vanish. Although the address is in its outward form to the Messenger ﷺ, what is meant is his community. He, ﷺ, was the furthest of all people from looking at the adornment of this world and the most attached to what is with Allah, and he said regarding the world: "Cursed is the world, cursed is what is in it, except what is sought for the sake of Allah." He was very strict in prohibiting being deceived by this world and looking at its adornment. ﴿And do not extend﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131] is more emphatic than "do not look," because extending the gaze implies continuing and admiring, unlike a mere look, which may not involve that. The eye itself is not extended, so it is an elision of a noun: ﴿do not extend﴾ [al-Hijr: 88] the gaze of ﴿your two eyes﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131], and a glance that is not extended is forgiven, like one who unexpectedly encounters something and then lowers his gaze. Looking at adornments is fixed in human nature, so whoever sees something of them loves to keep gazing at it. The pious have been very strict about lowering the gaze from the buildings of the oppressors and the possessions of the wicked, whether mounts, garments, or others, because they only acquire them so that the eyes of onlookers may see them and so that they may take pride in them. So whoever looks at them fulfills their aim and is in effect encouraging them to acquire them. ﴿Azwaajan﴾ is in the accusative as an object, and the meaning is: categories of disbelievers. And ﴿minhum﴾ is in the position of a qualifier for ﴿azwaajan﴾, meaning: categories and groups of disbelievers, as He said: ﴿and others of its kind in pairs﴾ [Sad: 58]. Al-Zamakhshari permitted that ﴿azwaajan﴾ be accusative as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in ﴿bihi﴾, with ﴿matta'na﴾ as its verb, the object being ﴿minhum﴾, as if it were said: to that with which We gave enjoyment, which is categories of some of them, and some people among them. ﴿Zahrata﴾ is accusative as a term of blame, or a second object of ﴿matta'na﴾ by implying the meaning of "given," or a substitute for the place of the prepositional phrase, or a substitute for ﴿azwaajan﴾ on the assumption of "those possessing the flower," or making ﴿zahrata﴾ as an intensification, or accusative by a verb omitted that is indicated by ﴿matta'na﴾, meaning: We made for them ﴿zahrata﴾, or a circumstantial clause from the pronoun, or it is in the case where the tanwin of ﴿zahrata﴾ is dropped because of two consecutive unvocalized letters, and the predicate of ﴿al-hayat﴾ is as a substitute for ﴿ma﴾. All of these grammatical analyses are transmitted, and the last was chosen by Makki, who rejected its being a substitute for the place of ﴿ma﴾, because it would involve separating, by the substitute, between the relative clause, which is ﴿matta'na﴾ and its complement, ﴿li-naftinahum﴾, so the substitute ﴿zahrata﴾ ...

﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.﴾ That is, what has been stored up for them of gifts in the Hereafter is ﴿better﴾ than what these people have been given to enjoy in this world, and ﴿more enduring﴾, that is, more lasting. It has been said: what He provides them, even if little, is better than what they have been given, even if abundant in ornament, and the sanctity of this. It has been said: it refers to what you have been given of prophethood and Islam. It has been said: it refers to what Allah grants the believers of lands and spoils. It has been said: it refers to contentment. It has been said: it refers to Allah's reward for patience and for indifference to the world.

When Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to glorify Him at those appointed times, and forbade him to extend his gaze toward what the disbelievers have been given to enjoy, He commanded him to order his family to pray, which after the testimony of faith is the most emphatic of the pillars of Islam. He commanded him to be steadfast in persisting in it despite its hardships, and not to be distracted from it. Allah informed him that he should not ask Him to provide for himself, nor strive to obtain provision and toil at it, but rather commanded him to empty his heart for the matter of the Hereafter. His address to him, peace be upon him, includes his community.

The majority read ﴿narzuquka﴾ with a damma on the qaf. A group, among them Ibn Wathhab, read it with the qaf assimilated into the kaf. This is reported from Ya'qub. The author of al-Lawami' said: Abu 'Amr refrained from assimilating a similar form after assimilating ﴿narzuqukum﴾ and the like, because the kaf there falls at the end of the word and is a letter of pause. If it were vowelled in pause, its pausing would be on a vowel, which would be a departure from their speech. If he were to indicate the fatha, the fatha would be too light to be partially expressed; rather, the expression of part of it is like the expression of all of it. If he were to make it sukun, it would strip the letter of its sound. Perhaps whoever assimilated took the path of those who say (as with) Ja'far and 'Amir and tafa''ala, so that it is doubled in pause, or it is assimilated on condition that one does not pause in any case, so the end becomes like the medial position. End of quotation.

﴿Al-'aqibah﴾, that is, the praiseworthy end, or the good outcome, belongs to the people of piety.

﴿They said: Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ This was their habit in demanding signs, as if they regarded the signs that had appeared as not being signs, so they demanded what they chose, in keeping with their custom of obstinacy. They were answered with His words:

﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the earlier scriptures?﴾ That is, the Qur'an, which preceded (as) the good tidings, and by My revelation to the Messengers of it in the earlier divine books that were sent down to the Messengers. The Qur'an is the greatest of signs in its inimitability, and it is the sign that remains until the Day of Resurrection. In this interrogation there is a rebuke for them.

Nafi', Abu 'Amr and Hafs read ﴿ta'tihim﴾ with a ta', in agreement with the word bayyinah. The rest of the Seven, Abu Bahriyya, Ibn Muhaysin, Talha, Ibn Abi Layla, Ibn Munadhir, Khalaf, Abu 'Ubayda, Ibn Sa'dan, Ibn 'Isa and Ibn Jubayr al-Antaki read (ya'tihim) with a ya', because the sign is feminine only metaphorically, and because of the intervening separation.

The majority read (bayyinatu) as annexed to (ma). A group, among them Abu Zayd from Abu 'Amr, read it with tanwin, and (ma) as an apposition. The author of al-Lawami' said: It is possible that (ma) is a negation, and by that is meant what is in the Qur'an of abrogating (naskh) material and of distinction which was not in other books.

A group read (bayyinatan) with a fatha and tanwin, with (ma) as the subject of ﴿ta'tihim﴾, and (bayyinatan) being in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). Whoever read ya'tihim with a ya' does so in keeping with the wording of (ma), and whoever read with a ta' observes the meaning, because they are diverse things and the knowledge of those who passed and what God wills.

The majority read ﴿fi al-suhuf﴾ with a damma on the ha', while a group, among them Ibn 'Abbas, read it with the ha' quiescent. The pronoun in (dammana) before it refers to the bayyinah, because it carries the sense of proof and evidence, as al-Zamakhshari said. The apparent reference is to the Messenger, peace be upon him, because of their saying: ﴿Why did you not send to us a messenger?﴾ For this reason some of them estimated it as before the sending of Muhammad to them.

﴿Humiliation and disgrace﴾ are linked with the torment of the Hereafter. It has been said: (nadhilla) refers to the world and (nakhza) to the Hereafter. It has been said: humiliation (dhull) is abasement and disgrace (khizy) is exposure.

The majority read ﴿nadhilla wa-nakhza﴾ in the active voice, while Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, Zayd ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan in the narration of 'Abbad, al-'Umari, Dawud, al-Fazari, Abu Hatim and Ya'qub read it in the passive voice.

﴿Say: Each is waiting, so wait.﴾ That is, awaiting the outcome of the matter, from us and from you. In this is a threat and a warning to them. He used the predicate ﴿waiting﴾ in the singular, taking into account the wording of (kull), as in His words: ﴿Say: each acts according to his manner﴾ [Al-Isra': 84]. Al-tarabbus is patience and waiting for relief. (Man ashab) is a subject and predicate, to which (fa-sata'lamun) is suspended. Al-Farra' permitted that (ma) be a relative pronoun meaning "who", so that it is the object of (fa-sata'lamun), and (ashab) is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimate being "the one who are the companions of". This accords with the school of the Kufans, for they permit the omission of such a pronoun absolutely, whether or not there is length in the relative clause, and whether the relative is (ayy) or other.

The majority read ﴿al-sawiyy﴾ on the pattern fa'il, that is, "the even". Abu Mijlaz and 'Imran ibn Hudayr read (al-sawa'), that is, the middle. Al-Jahdari and Ibn Ya'mar read (al-su'a), on the pattern fu'la, feminine because of the feminine (al-sirat), and it is among what is masculine and feminine, feminine like (al-as'a') from (al-su'a), contrary to guidance, paired with (wa-man ihtada) in opposition. Its meaning: (fa-sata'lamun), O disbelievers, who is upon error and who is upon guidance. This is supported by Ibn 'Abbas's reading ﴿al-sirat al-su'﴾. It is reported from both of them that they read (al-su'a) on the pattern fu'la. It is possible that its original form is (al-suwwa), since it is reported from them, so the hamza was lightened by changing it to waw and assimilated. It is also possible that fu'la is from (al-sawa'), its ya' changed to waw and the waw assimilated into waw. Analogically, when fu'la is formed from (al-sawa'), it would become (al-suwya), so a waw and a ya' would come together, and one of them preceded by sukun, so the waw becomes ya' and is assimilated into the ya', so the form would be (al-sayya). (Suwayy) was also read with a damma on the sin, a fatha on the waw and a shadda on the ya', as a diminutive of (al-su'), as al-Zamakhshari said, but this is not good, for if it were a diminutive of (su') its hamza would remain in the diminutive, and you would say (su'yi). The better view is that it is a diminutive of (sawa'), as they said of (ata') "utayy". Whoever read (al-su'a) or (al-su') has in that a contrast with His words ﴿and who is guided﴾. In the majority's reading, the contrast is not observed in the interrogative.

* *

Surat al-Anbiya', peace be upon them, one hundred and twelve verses, Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

[Al-Anbiya': 1] ﴿Their reckoning has drawn near to mankind, while they are heedless and turning away.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 2] ﴿No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while playing.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 3] ﴿Their hearts are distracted. And they conspire in secret, those who did wrong: "Is this not but a human like yourselves? Will you then submit to sorcery while you see?"﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 4] ﴿He said: My Lord knows every word in the heaven and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 5] ﴿Rather they say: "Confused dreams! Rather he has invented it! Rather he is a poet! Let him bring us a sign as the earlier ones were sent."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 6] ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed. Will they then believe?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 7] ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed; so ask the people of the reminder if you do not know.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 8] ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 9] ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 10] ﴿We have indeed sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder. Will you not then understand?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 11] ﴿How many a town that did wrong have We broken, and raised after it another people.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 12] ﴿When they perceived Our might, behold, they were fleeing from it.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 13] ﴿"Do not flee, but return to what you were made to enjoy and your dwellings, that you may be questioned."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 14] ﴿They said: "Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 15] ﴿That claim of theirs did not cease until We made them a mown field, extinguished.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 16] ﴿We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 17] ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were to do so.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 18] ﴿Rather We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 19] ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and those with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 20] ﴿They glorify by night and day, never flagging.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 21] ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 22] ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, both would have been corrupted. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 23] ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 24] ﴿Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say: "Bring your proof. This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me." Rather most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 25] ﴿We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 26] ﴿They said: "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather they are honoured servants.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 27] ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 28] ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one with whom He is pleased, and they are fearful of His awe.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 29] ﴿Whoever among them says, "I am a god besides Him," that We shall recompense with Hell. Thus We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 30] ﴿Have not those who disbelieved seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them, and made every living thing from water? Will they not then believe?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 31] ﴿We placed firm mountains in the earth lest it shake with them, and We made in it wide paths, that they may be guided.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 32] ﴿We made the heaven a protected roof, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 33] ﴿It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each swimming in an orbit.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 34] ﴿We did not grant immortality to any human before you. If you die, will they be the immortals?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 35] ﴿Every soul shall taste death, and We test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 36] ﴿When those who disbelieved see you, they take you only in mockery: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" While they are disbelievers in the mention of the Most Merciful.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 37] ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 38] ﴿They say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 39] ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped!﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 40] ﴿Rather it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 41] ﴿Messengers before you were indeed mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to mock.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 42] ﴿Say: "Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?" Rather they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 43] ﴿Or do they have gods that defend them from Us? They cannot help themselves, nor are they accompanied by Us.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 44] ﴿Rather We gave these people and their fathers enjoyment until life was prolonged for them. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges? Are they then the victors?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 45] ﴿Say: "I only warn you by revelation," but the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.﴾

[Al-Anbiya': 10] ﴿We have indeed sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder. Will you not then understand?﴾

[Al-Anbiya': 12] ﴿When they perceived Our might, behold, they were fleeing from it.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 13] ﴿"Do not flee, but return to what you were made to enjoy and your dwellings, that you may be questioned."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 14] ﴿They said: "Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 15] ﴿That claim of theirs did not cease until We made them a mown field, extinguished.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 16] ﴿We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 17] ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were to do so.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 18] ﴿Rather We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 19] ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and those with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 20] ﴿They glorify by night and day, never flagging.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 21] ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 22] ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, both would have been corrupted. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾

[Al-Anbiya': 27] ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 28] ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one with whom He is pleased, and they are fearful of His awe.﴾

[Al-Anbiya': 31] ﴿We placed firm mountains in the earth lest it shake with them, and We made in it wide paths, that they may be guided.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 32] ﴿We made the heaven a protected roof, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 33] ﴿It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each swimming in an orbit.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 34] ﴿We did not grant immortality to any human before you. If you die, will they be the immortals?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 35] ﴿Every soul shall taste death, and We test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned.﴾

[Al-Anbiya': 37] ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 38] ﴿They say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 39] ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped!﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 40] ﴿Rather it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 41] ﴿Messengers before you were indeed mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to mock.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 42] ﴿Say: "Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?" Rather they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 43] ﴿Or do they have gods that defend them from Us? They cannot help themselves, nor are they accompanied by Us.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 44] ﴿Rather We gave these people and their fathers enjoyment until life was prolonged for them. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges? Are they then the victors?﴾

This accords with the school of the Kufans, for they permit the omission of such a pronoun absolutely, whether or not there is length in the relative clause, and whether the relative is (ayy) or other.

The majority read ﴿al-sawiyy﴾ on the pattern fa'il, that is, "the even". Abu Mijlaz and 'Imran ibn Hudayr read (al-sawa'), that is, the middle. Al-Jahdari and Ibn Ya'mar read (al-su'a), on the pattern fu'la, feminine because of the feminine (al-sirat), and it is among what is masculine and feminine, feminine like (al-as'a') from (al-su'a), contrary to guidance, paired with (wa-man ihtada) in opposition. Its meaning: (fa-sata'lamun), O disbelievers, who is upon error and who is upon guidance. This is supported by Ibn 'Abbas's reading ﴿al-sirat al-su'﴾. It is reported from both of them that they read (al-su'a) on the pattern fu'la. It is possible that its original form is (al-suwwa), since it is reported from them, so the hamza was lightened by changing it to waw and assimilated. It is also possible that fu'la is from (al-sawa'), its ya' changed to waw and the waw assimilated into waw. Analogically, when fu'la is formed from (al-sawa'), it would become (al-suwya), so a waw and a ya' would come together, and one of them preceded by sukun, so the waw becomes ya' and is assimilated into the ya', so the form would be (al-sayya). (Suwayy) was also read with a damma on the sin, a fatha on the waw and a shadda on the ya', as a diminutive of (al-su'), as al-Zamakhshari said, but this is not good, for if it were a diminutive of (su') its hamza would remain in the diminutive, and you would say (su'yi). The better view is that it is a diminutive of (sawa'), as they said of (ata') "utayy". Whoever read (al-su'a) or (al-su') has in that a contrast with His words ﴿and who is guided﴾. In the majority's reading, the contrast is not observed in the interrogative.

Surat al-Anbiya', peace be upon them, one hundred and twelve verses, Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

[Al-Anbiya': 1] ﴿Their reckoning has drawn near to mankind, while they are heedless and turning away.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 2] ﴿No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while playing.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 3] ﴿Their hearts are distracted. And they conspire in secret, those who did wrong: "Is this not but a human like yourselves? Will you then submit to sorcery while you see?"﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 4] ﴿He said: My Lord knows every word in the heaven and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 5] ﴿Rather they say: "Confused dreams! Rather he has invented it! Rather he is a poet! Let him bring us a sign as the earlier ones were sent."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 6] ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed. Will they then believe?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 7] ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed; so ask the people of the reminder if you do not know.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 8] ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 9] ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 10] ﴿We have indeed sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder. Will you not then understand?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 11] ﴿How many a town that did wrong have We broken, and raised after it another people.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 12] ﴿When they perceived Our might, behold, they were fleeing from it.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 13] ﴿"Do not flee, but return to what you were made to enjoy and your dwellings, that you may be questioned."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 14] ﴿They said: "Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 15] ﴿That claim of theirs did not cease until We made them a mown field, extinguished.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 16] ﴿We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 17] ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were to do so.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 18] ﴿Rather We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 19] ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and those with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 20] ﴿They glorify by night and day, never flagging.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 21] ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 22] ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, both would have been corrupted. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 23] ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 24] ﴿Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say: "Bring your proof. This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me." Rather most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 25] ﴿We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 26] ﴿They said: "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather they are honoured servants.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 27] ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 28] ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one with whom He is pleased, and they are fearful of His awe.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 29] ﴿Whoever among them says, "I am a god besides Him," that We shall recompense with Hell. Thus We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 30] ﴿Have not those who disbelieved seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them, and made every living thing from water? Will they not then believe?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 31] ﴿We placed firm mountains in the earth lest it shake with them, and We made in it wide paths, that they may be guided.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 32] ﴿We made the heaven a protected roof, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 33] ﴿It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each swimming in an orbit.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 34] ﴿We did not grant immortality to any human before you. If you die, will they be the immortals?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 35] ﴿Every soul shall taste death, and We test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 36] ﴿When those who disbelieved see you, they take you only in mockery: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" While they are disbelievers in the mention of the Most Merciful.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 37] ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 38] ﴿They say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 39] ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped!﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 40] ﴿Rather it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 41] ﴿Messengers before you were indeed mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to mock.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 42] ﴿Say: "Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?" Rather they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 43] ﴿Or do they have gods that defend them from Us? They cannot help themselves, nor are they accompanied by Us.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 44] ﴿Rather We gave these people and their fathers enjoyment until life was prolonged for them. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges? Are they then the victors?﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 45] ﴿Say: "I only warn you by revelation," but the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 46] ﴿If a breath of the punishment of your Lord touches them, they will surely say, "Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers."﴾
[Al-Anbiya': 47] ﴿We shall set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything; and if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And sufficient are We as reckoners.﴾

[p. 294] Al-qasm: breaking a hard thing until the coherence of its parts becomes visible. Al-rakd: striking the animal with the leg. Khamadat al-nar: the fire was extinguished. Damaghahu: he struck his brain, like "kabidahu" (he struck his liver) and "ra'isahu" (he struck his head). Rataqa al-shay': he sealed it, and it became closed; from this comes al-ratqa', for a woman whose vagina is closed. Fataqa: he separated what was joined. Al-fajj: the wide path. Al-sabh: swimming. Kalaahu: he guarded it, yakla'uhu kilaa'atan. It is said: go in Allah's protection (kila'at Allah), and iktala'tu minhu: I took care to guard against it. Ibn Harma said:

Indeed Sulaymā, and Allah guards her, has withheld from what would have harmed her.

Al-nafkha: a step. And "nafakha lahu min 'atayahu": he gave him a sufficient share of his gifts. The poet said:

When a rabdah, from whatever direction it blows upon him,
its breezes, a friend who keeps close to him.

Al-khardal: a well-known seed (mustard).
